summary: Import-time outbound fetch to mutable author-controlled GitHub raw URL
details: On every require() of the package's main entry, lib/index.js performs a top-level fetch to https://raw.githubusercontent.com/alannzxd/xclient/refs/heads/main/information.json (a mutable main-branch raw URL on the author's personal repo) and console.logs a message field from the response. The fetched JSON is only printed — it is not eval'd, executed, or written to disk — and no installer-side data (env vars, credentials, host info) is included in the request, so this is a usage/announcement beacon rather than exfiltration or remote code execution. The package is also a fork of the well-known WhatsApp library `baileys`, with no obvious installer-harm payload beyond this beacon. Concerns worth a human review: (a) require-time outbound network breaks offline / air-gapped / sandboxed environments, (b) the source is an author-mutable raw GitHub URL — today's benign JSON message can be changed by the author at any time without a package republish, and if any future consumer change ever feeds the response into an interpreter the risk profile shifts immediately, (c) the behavior is undisclosed and has no opt-out. The preinstall hook is a benign Node.js >=20 engine version check with no network or filesystem side effects.
